name: Bali
headline: First passport stamp in island light.
subheadline: A quick visual note from Canggu, Ubud, and Uluwatu.
introduction: A short Bali overview for the photo page: soft mornings, green inland roads, cliff light, and a slower island pace.
shortDescription: A short Bali overview: cafe mornings, rice-field roads, cliff views, and soft sunset light.
description: My first trip abroad: digital nomad friends, Galungan days, mall food survival, and a chaotic first passport stamp.
longDescription: A short Bali overview for the photo page.
overview:
Bali was my first trip abroad, so everything felt a little bigger than usual: the air, the roads, and the small courage of talking to strangers. I first knew Bali through the digital nomad community, and somehow came home with a few first international friends.

The food and I did not get along very well, so instant noodles and mall food quietly carried me through the trip. I was also lucky to be there during Galungan, a sacred Balinese Hindu celebration of Dharma winning over Adharma. A good first stamp on the passport, with a little chaos included.
weatherNote: Dry season is easier for road days. Short rain can still happen, so keep the plan loose.
travelTips: Do not stack Canggu, Ubud, and Uluwatu into one day.
Add buffer time for traffic, especially around sunset.
Carry a light sarong or cover-up for temples.
Pick accommodation by area, not only by room photos.
notFor: A trip where every hour needs to be tightly scheduled.
Travelers who dislike traffic or moving between areas.

images.title: Arch Over the Breaking Swell
images.story: The tide was hammering against the hollow under Batu Bolong, sending white spray high up the dark basalt cliff. Tall bamboo penjors were already bending in the ocean breeze above the arch, signaling ceremony season across the island. Leaning over the lookout railing with my camera, it finally hit me that I was standing in another country.

images.title: Guardian with the Feathered Spear
images.story: The afternoon heat on the flagstones was fierce, but the dancers held their posture without flinching. She stood perfectly still balancing the feathered standard while the rhythm picked up from the gamelan circle behind her. Watching them move made the chaotic scooter ride through southern traffic feel immediately worthwhile.

images.title: Legong Dancer in Purple Silk
images.story: Every snap of her painted fan landed squarely on a strike from the bronze metallophones behind her. The purple and gold silk caught the afternoon glare as she shifted weight, completely tuned out of the crowd circling the pavilion. I lost track of time trying to time my shutter with her sharp eye movements.

images.title: Galungan Arches Along the Alley
images.story: Tall bamboo penjors arched toward each other from every storefront, turning the market lane into a green tunnel for Galungan. Between dodging oncoming scooters and glancing at souvenir stalls, I kept craning my neck up at the woven palm tassels. After another convenience store lunch back at the room, walking into that lively street was an easy cure.

images.title: Orange Streamer on Woven Bamboo
images.story: Looking straight up, the curved bamboo pole looked like a golden spine reaching into the cloudless sky. The orange streamer snapped in the breeze right beside the carved black volcanic stone of the temple gate. Every family crafts their own penjor from scratch, marking the holiday with palm fronds bending toward the street.

images.title: Colossus in Green Patina
images.story: Standing at the base of the pedestal made me feel minuscule, squinting up at twenty-eight stories of welded copper and brass. The midday sun lit up Vishnu’s golden crown while Garuda’s weathered green wings spread wide into the clear blue. Seeing the sheer scale in person after reading about it for years made the sticky heat easy to ignore.

images.title: Coconut Shells Along the Paddy
images.story: Dozens of dried coconut shells hung along the fence wire like an improvised alarm for the rice field. Across the bright green stalks, a two-story villa hoisted a red kite flag under the morning clouds. Walking past, I realized half the charm of the island was finding clever, handmade solutions everywhere you looked.

images.title: Garuda Looming Over the Plaza
images.story: Standing on the pale plaza at Garuda Wisnu Kencana, the massive copper wings looked heavy enough to bend the sky. The sheer height of Vishnu perched on his mythical mount made every person below look like a wandering speck. Under the midday haze, the green patina gave the metal a quiet, weathered weight.

images.title: Kite Runners in the Field
images.story: Two boys waded waist-deep through the rice crop, trailing long strings and waiting for a gust of wind. The low golden hour sun lit the tips of the stalks and set the rooftop tiles glowing behind the palms. Watching them sprint barefoot through the mud was far more entertaining than any organized tour.

images.title: Distant Volcano Across the Water
images.story: A pale strip of volcano peeked out from behind the sea clouds, so faint it almost blended into the sky. A swallow swooped across the empty sand while two sunbathers soaked up the midday heat near the water. Out on the horizon, fishing boats sat dead still on the flat surface.

images.title: Stone Path Through Deep Canopy
images.story: The stone slabs cut a narrow channel into the forest, with thick foliage leaning in from both sides. Morning light only managed to break through in a few patchy pools on the pavement. The air was cool and smelled of damp earth, offering a welcome break from the humid coast.

images.title: Wings Spread in the Treetop
images.story: A white egret flared its wings wide, steadying itself on a flimsy branch above the village canopy. Several others were already perched quietly among the dark leaves, waiting out the late afternoon breeze. Against the pale sky, the tree looked like it was growing white feathers instead of fruit.

images.title: Pale Petals on Dark Water
images.story: A pale peach water lily sat wide open over the dark pond, each petal beaded with morning drizzle. I stopped beside the stone basin between temples to catch my breath in the rising humidity. In a place where motorbikes never stopped humming, the quiet surface felt like a rare pause button.

images.title: Carved Guardian in Cool Shades
images.story: Tucked between rolled bamboo screens, someone had outfitted this mossy stone guardian with dark sunglasses, a wristwatch, and a cigarette. Fresh marigolds and frangipani blossoms rested across his lap, turning daily temple offerings into an affectionate joke. It felt like an oddly fitting farewell mascot on my final afternoon on the island.
